description:
## Why

`pkix-ac` is at version 0.0.0 — pure skeleton. `AttributeCertificate` wraps a `Vec<u8>` of DER bytes (not actually parsed). `validate_attribute_cert()` is a const fn returning `Err(Error::AaPathInvalid(NoTrustedPath))` unconditionally. RFC 5755 §5 algorithm not implemented.

Real-world need: attribute certificates carry authorization claims (group membership, role, clearance) without re-issuing the holder's public-key cert. Used in some federation deployments, government PKI, and S/MIME advanced cases.

## What

Build out pkix-ac:

1. **AttributeCertificate parsing** — RFC 5755 §4.1. Wraps the Holder, Issuer, AttCertValidityPeriod, and an Extensions sequence. Use `x509-cert` for the underlying ASN.1 building blocks; `AttributeCertificate` is its own SEQUENCE.
2. **Holder identification** — RFC 5755 §4.2.2. Holder can be: `baseCertificateID` (issuer + serial of holder's PKC), `entityName` (a GeneralNames), or `objectDigestInfo` (hash of holder's pubkey/cert/object). All three need parsing.
3. **AttributeCertIssuer (AA) chain validation** — RFC 5755 §5. The Attribute Authority signs the AC; its own cert chain must be validated independently (typically via pkix-path with an AA-specific trust set).
4. **AttributeCertificateValidity** check — like a regular cert's notBefore/notAfter, but a separate type per RFC 5755.
5. **Holder-PKC binding** — when Holder is `baseCertificateID` or `objectDigestInfo`, verify the AC's holder reference matches the actual PKC presented.
6. **Attribute extraction** — public API for callers to read the attributes after validation passes.

## Recommended decomposition (file children when work starts)

1. AttributeCertificate ASN.1 struct + parser (~150 lines).
2. Holder identification + binding check (~80 lines).
3. Attribute-cert validity + AA chain validation (~80 lines).
4. Public API for attribute extraction (~50 lines).
5. CRL revocation for ACs (RFC 5755 §6) — ACs have their own CRL profile; the existing pkix-revocation::CrlChecker likely needs an AC-aware variant. Separate sub-bead.

## Acceptance

- [ ] AttributeCertificate parse round-trips (parse + re-encode → identical DER).
- [ ] Real-world AC test vectors validate (pyca/cryptography may have some; or generate via openssl).
- [ ] Holder binding tested against three Holder shapes.
- [ ] AA chain validated via pkix-path (compose with that crate; do not duplicate path-walking logic).
- [ ] Crate published.

## Out of scope

- AC issuance.
- Specific attribute taxonomies (group membership, clearance) — that's application-policy.
- ACL/AC-based authorization enforcement — caller's job.

## Effort

~600 lines + tests across the children. 2-3 days.

## Filed as

Low-impact gap per audit. Lower priority than pkix-ct because attribute certs are a niche feature in modern PKI.
notes:
Decomposed 2026-05-10 into 5 child beads:
- PKIX-ng0x.1 (P3): RFC 5755 §4.1 AttributeCertificate ASN.1 parser + round-trip
- PKIX-ng0x.2 (P3): RFC 5755 §4.2.2 Holder identification + binding check (depends on .1)
- PKIX-ng0x.3 (P3): AttCertValidityPeriod + AA chain validation (depends on .1, .2)
- PKIX-ng0x.4 (P3): attribute extraction public API (depends on .3)
- PKIX-ng0x.5 (P4): RFC 5755 §6 AC CRL revocation (depends on .3)
The matching of children to the recommended decomposition in this bead's original description is one-to-one. Each child is small enough to fit one focused session. Total estimate (~600 LOC) preserved across children. Only PKIX-ng0x.1 is currently ready.
title: pkix-ac: real RFC 5755 attribute certificate validation
